To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution and contents of key mRNAs in lysosomes are altered in the earliest stages, i.e. initial lesions and fatty streaks, of atherosclerotisis.

the changes in lysosomes in the early stages of atherosclerosis may be a result of a disturbance in the balance of endosome‐to‐lysosome trafficking and/or in the lysosomal degradation of the lipoproteins and that these changes may be the cause of the development of fatty streaks and atherosclerotics.
the changes in lysosomes are involved in the earliest stages and may be a part of the pathomechanism of atherosclerosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
changes of lysosomes during atherosclerosis.
the role of lysosomal changes in the earliest stages in the development of atherogenesis.
the earliest changes in the lysosomes of intimal cells in atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes occurring in lysosomal compartments in atherosclerosis are complex and are not limited to a simple lysosomal dysfunction.

the lysosomal changes in the early stages of atherosclerosis are not due to a deficiency of enzymes, but are due to a change in the lysosomal membrane permeability, which leads to the accumulation of lipids in lysosomes and thus to their transformation into foam cells.
the changes in the lysosomal compartment, including the changes of the lysosomal enzymes, may be a cause and/or consequence of atherogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the changes in the lysosomes of the earliest atherosclerotics lesions are characterized by the increased number of lysosomes, increased contents of CD68 mRNA, and the decreased contents of EEA and Rab5a mRNA.
the changes in lysosomes in initial lesions may be due to the changes of the lysosomal membrane permeability, which may be caused by the changes of the composition of the lysosomal proteins.

lysosome changes in the initial lesion of atherosclerosis are characterized by the accumulation of lipids, and the increase of the number of lysosomes, and the changes in the lysosome distribution pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lysosomal system is involved in the development of atherogenesis, which may have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
lysosomes are the main players in atherosclerosis and that the changes occurring in them are important for the understanding of the disease. © 2016 The Authors.
lysosomes in atherogenesis are not only a target for the action of atherogenic factors but also play a role in the development of atherogenesis.
